summary: Guernsey customary law restricts what you can leave of Guernsey real property, but movables are free. Trusts are well established and foundations are available. The Hague Trusts Convention was extended to Guernsey.
reserved_share: Heirs have rights over immovable (real) property under Guernsey customary law and the Law Reform (Property) (Guernsey) Law 1979; movables are free. The fractions were not confirmed.
foreign_law_note: Movables follow the law of the deceased's domicile, immovables in Guernsey follow Guernsey law. There is no choice of nationality law.
trust_note: Trusts (Guernsey) Law 2007 and Hague Convention extended to Guernsey (1 July 1993 per a Dutch treaty record). Foundations (Guernsey) Law 2012 allows private foundations. No local tax on foreign trusts was checked.
open_questions: The HCCH status-table page could be read only in an older cached version that does not show territorial extensions; extension dates come from the UK Treaty Series 14 (1992) and a Dutch treaty record, and should be re-checked on hcch.net.
Exact forced heirship rules for Guernsey real property and any recent reform.
